title: Importance of Timely Salah
summary: Salah is a crucial obligation for all Muslims, and neglecting it deliberately is a grave sin, comparable to other major sins like theft or adultery. Muslims are urged to perform Salah on time, and if missed, to perform it as soon as possible. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) instructed that missed prayers should be performed once remembered. To compensate for past missed prayers, Muslims should perform Qada Salah with specific or general intentions, continuing until all missed prayers are accounted for. Effort and supplication are vital, as no other expiation exists except for fulfilling these missed prayers unless someone dies unable to perform them, in which case Fidya may be considered.
translation: It is extremely important for every accountable Muslim man and woman to perform Salah. As long as a person does not perform Salah, they remain accountable for it. Scholars agree that deliberately neglecting obligatory Salah is a grave sin comparable to, or even greater than, committing adultery, theft, or consuming alcohol. Therefore, Muslims must make an effort to perform each Salah on time, and if missed, perform it at the earliest opportunity. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that if someone forgets a Salah, they should perform it as soon as they remember. Another hadith mentions that if someone forgets or sleeps through a Salah, they should compensate by praying once they recall. This hadith is found in Sahih Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, and Tirmidhi. It's important not to make a habit of deliberately skipping or delaying Salah, as this is a major sin. If one has missed Salah in their life, they should strive to perform Qada for it, praying with the intention that covers specific missed prayers if known, or generally if not. For example, 'I am performing Qada for the Fajr missed last Friday,' or 'I am performing the earliest missed Dhuhr.' Continue until all are accounted for. Attempt to perform five daily prayers, and include Qada alongside. If unable, ensure performing at least one Qada daily. Efforts and supplication will lead to ease. No other expiation exists outside of performing the missed prayers unless one dies in a state of incapacity. In that case, ransom (Fidya) can be considered, but if neither was performed nor instructed, accountability remains.
